subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic durable group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, memory, and per-user skill/config boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful but crosses durable agent creation, private memory, group routing, tool permissions, cost/resource governance, and plugin API/config surfaces that source inspection cannot safely choose for maintainers.

options.title: Design a generic opt-in contract first
options.body: Add or specify a channel/runtime identity-to-agent lifecycle seam, then let Feishu implement it with explicit admin policy, memory namespaces, TTL/quotas, and migration/docs/tests.

options.title: Keep it Feishu-local and narrow
options.body: Extend only the Feishu plugin from existing groupSessionScope and dynamicAgentCreation primitives, accepting a channel-specific contract and narrower future reuse.

options.title: Reject automatic group subagents for now
options.body: Keep current group_sender sessions and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported path until stronger demand or a broader architecture proposal appears.

recommendation.title: Design a generic opt-in contract first
recommendation.body: Add or specify a channel/runtime identity-to-agent lifecycle seam, then let Feishu implement it with explicit admin policy, memory namespaces, TTL/quotas, and migration/docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names @m1heng as the Feishu community maintainer, and this decision is primarily about Feishu product behavior plus its channel/plugin boundary.
